sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Broad sector breadth remains extremely narrow with only 2 of 11 groups all-green, anchored by Energy's dominant leadership while Communication Services collapses to the bottom of the board.

Energy (0.900 momentum) and Healthcare (0.733 momentum) stand as the lone all-green sectors across week, month, quarter, half, and year-to-date timeframes. Energy continues to exhibit sustained multi-month dominance, holding the #1 rank across the board, followed closely by Technology at 0.800 momentum. 

Defensive and low-tier groups are seeing minor positioning shifts, but momentum remains concentrated at the very top. Utilities and Consumer Cyclical eked out 1-spot improvements over the last five sessions, yet both remain mired in the bottom third of the market. Meanwhile, Communication Services is actively fading, sliding 2 spots to land in last place with a market-low momentum score of 0.067.

## Strength
- Energy is the clear market leader with a 0.900 momentum score, ranking #1 year-to-date and demonstrating sustained strength across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons.
- Market breadth is highly restricted, with just 2 of 11 sectors qualifying as all-green: Energy (0.900) and Healthcare (0.733).
- Technology holds the second-highest momentum profile at 0.800 (rank 2 year-to-date), rounding out the core leadership group alongside Healthcare.

## Movers & Momentum
- Communication Services was the primary five-session decliner, dropping 2 spots to rank 11 with an isolated momentum score of 0.067.
- Consumer Cyclical and Utilities posted minor 5-session rank gains (+1 spot each), but both remain stuck in laggard territory at rank 10 (0.400 momentum) and rank 9 (0.367 momentum), respectively.
- Mid-tier momentum sits heavily compressed in the 0.40–0.57 range, spanning Industrials (0.450), Financials (0.450), Basic Materials (0.417), and Consumer Defensive (0.567).

## Divergences
- Laggard performance is concentrated in Real Estate (0.350 momentum, rank 8), Utilities (0.367 momentum, rank 9), and Communication Services (0.067 momentum, rank 11), creating a wide dispersion gap against top-tier leaders.
- No sectors are currently flagged for fragile all-green status, leaving Energy and Healthcare with uncompromised cross-timeframe performance profiles.

risk_radar.relative_strength: Energy is genuinely outperforming the S&P 500 with confirmed directional consistency (rs_score 0.83, rs_confirmed 0.83, beating SPY on 5/7 timeframes), while Technology displays high breadth by beating SPY on 6/7 timeframes (rs_score 0.83) but lacks sustained confirmation with an rs_confirmed of just 0.28. In addition, Basic Materials and Consumer Cyclical hit 20-session RS new highs, and Real Estate registered an RS cross turning positive against SPY despite beating the index on only 1/7 timeframes (rs_score 0.17, rs_confirmed 0.06).

- Healthcare and Utilities show deteriorating setups, each posting weak rs_confirmed readings of 0.17 and 0.11 against modest rs_scores of 0.50 and 0.33 while beating SPY on just 3/7 timeframes.
- Real Estate's fresh RS cross against SPY occurs on an exceptionally weak base, beating SPY on only 1/7 timeframes with an rs_score of 0.17 and rs_confirmed of 0.06.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Energy dominates absolute momentum while industrials and logistics surge, contrasted by sharp multi-timeframe breakdowns in manufacturing and materials.

Energy maintains a firm grip on leadership, with Oil & Gas E&P (momentum 0.866), Oil & Gas Drilling (0.838), and Oil & Gas Integrated (0.833) anchoring the top momentum tier. Breadth remains selective, with only 20 of 144 groups exhibiting all-green performance across all timeframes. Transport and commercial services are rotating aggressively higher, headlined by Rental & Leasing Services climbing 26 spots to rank 33 alongside strong 5-day gains in Integrated Freight & Logistics (+18 spots).

Conversely, severe drawdowns are hitting cyclical manufacturing and select defensive pockets. Textile Manufacturing experienced an outright collapse, plunging 119 spots to rank 141 with a weak 0.21 momentum score. Meanwhile, earlier leadership in segments like Healthcare Plans and Reinsurance is beginning to stall, showing early divergence as short-term rank slips despite nominally high momentum readings.

## Strength
- **Narrow All-Green Breadth:** Just 20 of 144 industry groups are positive across week, month, quarter, half, and YTD frames, led by Oil & Gas E&P (0.87 momentum), REIT - Hotel & Motel (0.86), and Diagnostics & Research (0.83).
- **Energy Cluster Leadership:** The space commands the top momentum rankings, with Oil & Gas Integrated holding rank 5 YTD (0.833 momentum), Oil & Gas Drilling at rank 6 YTD (0.838 momentum), and Oil & Gas E&P at rank 10 YTD (0.866 momentum).
- **Sustained Performers:** Groups maintaining top-36 positioning across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons include Software - Application, Household & Personal Products, Health Information Services, Business Equipment & Supplies, and Credit Services.

## Movers & Momentum
- **Rapid Short-Term Climbers:** Rental & Leasing Services gained 26 spots over 5 sessions to reach rank 33 (momentum 0.76), followed by Security & Protection Services (+21 spots to rank 54) and Integrated Freight & Logistics (+18 spots to rank 48).
- **Severe Momentum Drops:** Textile Manufacturing plunged 119 positions over 5 days to rank 141 (momentum 0.21), while Metal Fabrication dropped 33 spots to rank 83 (momentum 0.21) and Biotechnology lost 29 spots to rank 71 (momentum 0.49).
- **Bottom-Tier Laggards:** Advertising Agencies sit at the bottom of the market (momentum 0.041, rank 144 YTD), joined closely by Resorts & Casinos (momentum 0.083, rank 137 YTD) and Gambling (momentum 0.090, rank 143 YTD).

## Divergences
- **Fading High-Momentum Groups:** Early fatigue is appearing in Healthcare Plans (momentum 0.65, -8 spots in 5d), Insurance - Reinsurance (momentum 0.69, -7 spots in 5d), Lodging (momentum 0.67, -7 spots in 5d), and Medical Distribution (momentum 0.68, -6 spots in 5d).
- **Emerging Bottom Turnarounds:** Early short-term rank jumps despite sub-0.50 momentum include Coking Coal (+9 spots, momentum 0.50), Paper & Paper Products (+9 spots, momentum 0.48), Airlines (+8 spots, momentum 0.49), and Recreational Vehicles (+8 spots, momentum 0.39).
